title: The Channel Dash — Operation Cerberus
subtitle: English Channel · 11–13 February 1942
tz: British time · UTC+1 (German clocks one hour ahead)
footnote: British time (GMT+1; the German war diaries run one hour ahead). No source gives lat/lon fixes for this action — every position is reconstructed from named headlands, ranges and speeds, including the three mine strikes. Formation members are spread slightly so they don't overlap.

cerberus: Scharnhorst, Gneisenau and Prinz Eugen at Brest after eleven months of RAF bombing
Weighs two hours late after an air-raid alarm — led by Z29, six destroyers, then the torpedo boats
Off Ushant at 30 knots; Coastal Command's radar patrols have both failed
Past the Casquets and Alderney in the dark
North-west of Le Havre; the 2nd Torpedo Boat Flotilla joins; German jamming of British radar begins
Sighted off Le Touquet by Group Captain Beamish's Spitfire — who keeps radio silence until he lands
Off Cap Gris-Nez; the 5th Torpedo Boat Flotilla joins
South Foreland's 9.2-inch battery fires 33 rounds — all miss; MTBs attack at 12:23
Esmonde's six Swordfish attack off Gravelines — all shot down
Scharnhorst mined off the Scheldt; Ciliax shifts to Z29
Pizey's destroyers attack through the bomber melee; Worcester wrecked
Gneisenau mined off Terschelling; under way again after 30 minutes
Gneisenau and Prinz Eugen rejoin off Heligoland
Brunsbüttel locks; Gneisenau strikes a wreck going in
harwich: Exercising off Orford Ness when the alarm comes — ordered to intercept at 28 knots
Walpole drops out with a bearing failure; the rest cross the German minefield
Campbell's radar: contact at nine miles
Attack at 3,300 yards through bomb splashes; Worcester closes to 2,200 yards
dover: Five MTBs and two MGBs sail
Fires torpedoes at 4,000 yards through the E-boat screen — no hits
sealion: Withdraws seaward to charge batteries — the squadron passes unseen

cerberus.name: Vizeadmiral Otto Ciliax
cerberus.flagship: Scharnhorst, then Z29, then Hermann Schoemann
cerberus.bio: Ran three heavy ships through the Strait of Dover in daylight under a fighter umbrella planned by Galland, changing flagship twice when Scharnhorst was mined and Z29 disabled herself. A tactical triumph that ended the Atlantic surface war: Gneisenau never sailed again.

harwich.name: Captain Mark Pizey
harwich.bio: Took six twenty-year-old destroyers from an exercise off Orford Ness straight across a German minefield to attack battleships in daylight. All torpedoes missed; Worcester was nearly lost.
harwich.fate: Admiral Sir Mark Pizey; Commander-in-Chief Indian Navy 1951–55; died 1993.

dover.name: Lieutenant-Commander Nigel Pumphrey
dover.bio: Five MTBs and two gunboats against a battle squadron behind a screen of E-boats; fired at 4,000 yards under fire from everything the Germans had.

ships.name: Scharnhorst
extra: Under way again on the port engine, working up to 27 knots — 30 miles astern of the others
Second mine north of Terschelling: engines stop, 7° list, 1,000 tons of water

ships.name: HMS Worcester
extra: Six 11-inch and 8-inch hits, both boiler rooms out, 27 dead
Reaches Harwich under her own steam

ships.name: HMS Walpole
extra: Back to Harwich with a wiped bearing

strikes.name: Spitfire recce — Beamish sights the squadron
strikes.note: Group Captain Beamish and Wing Commander Boyd stumble on the ships off Le Touquet, keep radio silence and report only on landing at Kenley — Ramsay hears at 11:30

strikes.name: 825 Squadron — Esmonde's Swordfish
strikes.note: Six Swordfish with ten Spitfires of 72 Squadron as their only escort; all six shot down, 13 of 18 aircrew killed; Lt Cdr Eugene Esmonde's posthumous VC

strikes.name: Bomber Command's three waves
strikes.note: 242 sorties in low cloud; 39 aircraft find something to bomb, 15 are lost, nothing is hit

strikes.name: 217 Squadron Beauforts
strikes.note: Torpedo attacks on Prinz Eugen from 1,000 yards; further Beaufort attacks at 17:10, 18:00 and 18:05 — no hits

strikes.name: Operation Donnerkeil — Galland's umbrella
strikes.note: JG 2, JG 26 and JG 1 in relays from Brittany to Holland, 16 fighters overhead at all times; 22 Luftwaffe aircraft lost

torpedoes.note: Pumphrey's boats fire at 4,000 yards through the E-boat screen
The surviving Swordfish drop at close range; no hits
Worcester holds on to 2,200 yards and is smothered

engagements.note: Every gun in the squadron against six Swordfish and five MTBs
Gneisenau and Prinz Eugen wreck Worcester; Captain Fein ceases fire when she appears to be sinking

events: RAF raid on Brest: the squadron waits two hours at anchor
Sealion withdraws to charge batteries — the one submarine watching Brest
The squadron sails
Coastal Command's 'Stopper' Hudson lands with a failed radar; its relief finds nothing
Dawn patrol 'Habo' recalled for fog
German jamming blankets the south-coast radars
Swingate radar at Dover plots three large ships at 60 miles — taken for an air-sea rescue exercise
Beamish sees the ships — and says nothing until he lands
Ramsay at Dover learns the squadron is off Boulogne; Operation Fuller is ordered
South Foreland battery opens fire at 27,000 yards
Dover MTBs attack
Esmonde's Swordfish annihilated
Scharnhorst hits a mine off the Scheldt; Ciliax transfers to Z29
Harwich destroyers attack; Worcester hit six times
Z29 disabled by her own premature shell; Ciliax moves again, to Hermann Schoemann
Gneisenau mined off Terschelling
Scharnhorst's second mine: engines stopped, 1,000 tons flooding
Gneisenau and Prinz Eugen reach the Elbe
Scharnhorst limps into Wilhelmshaven
The Times: 'nothing more mortifying to the pride of sea-power has happened since the seventeenth century'

ports.name: Brest
ports.note: Home of the Brest Group since March 1941; bombed 300 times

ports.name: Le Havre
ports.note: 2nd Torpedo Boat Flotilla joins from here

ports.name: Brunsbüttel
ports.note: Kiel Canal locks — Gneisenau and Prinz Eugen's destination

ports.name: Schiphol
ports.note: JG 1 relays over the Dutch coast

ports.name: Dover
ports.note: MTBs, and the South Foreland 9.2-inch battery at Swingate

ports.name: Dover Castle — Vice-Admiral Dover
ports.note: Ramsay's headquarters; Operation Fuller had waited a year for this day and still failed

ports.name: Paris — Marinegruppe West
ports.note: Saalwächter's command; Hitler had insisted on a daylight passage of the Strait
